problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=\frac{{t}^{2}-1}{t}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}) \\  & =-12t+6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12t+6{t}^{2}) \\  & =-12+12t \\  & =12(t-1)\end{aligned}
$$
